title: Motion coherence discrimination (Britten et al.)
summary: How weak can a motion signal be and still have its direction seen? Random dots move, a varying share of them coherently, left or right (monkey set: along an example axis over a receptive field). The subject reports the direction: a monkey by a saccade to one of two targets, a person by an arrow key. The analysis fits a psychometric function. Comparing it with single MT neurons, the paper's main point, needs a recording this folder does not provide.
references: Britten, K. H., Shadlen, M. N., Newsome, W. T., & Movshon, J. A. (1992). The analysis of visual motion: A comparison of neuronal and psychophysical performance. Journal of Neuroscience, 12(12), 4745-4765.

deviations.original: Three rhesus monkeys reported the direction with a saccade to one of two LEDs (p. 4745, p. 4747)
deviations.here: configs/task.yaml: a person answers with an arrow key after the stimulus; fixation is asked for, not enforced
deviations.reason: A keyboard booth with no eye tracker; the monkey set (configs/task-monkey.yaml) keeps the saccade report

deviations.original: Aperture over the receptive field, motion axis along the neuron's preferred-null axis, speed at its preferred speed, chosen anew for every neuron (p. 4747)
deviations.here: Fixed values in each params file (example values in the monkey file, to be set for the neuron under study)
deviations.reason: No neuron is recorded by default; the files make the choice explicit instead of hiding it in code

deviations.original: Dots plotted one at a time at 6.67 kHz by a dedicated computer; each a 150-microsecond flash of a P4 phosphor (p. 4746)
deviations.here: Each display frame shows the dots plotted during that frame (density x 400 deg^2 / refresh rate), each visible for one frame
deviations.reason: A frame-based monitor cannot plot dots sequentially; the dot rate per unit area and time is kept

deviations.here: The nearest whole number of frames (3 frames = 50 ms at 60 Hz, 5 frames = 41.7 ms at 120 Hz); dx = speed x realised dt, so the speed is kept; signal_dt_ms is recorded on every trial
deviations.reason: Signal dots can only be displaced from a dot shown a whole number of frames earlier

deviations.original: A 31-bit hardware shift-register m-sequence, seeded per trial or with one fixed seed (p. 4747)
deviations.here: numpy's PCG64 generator seeded per trial (or one fixed seed); the seed is recorded on every trial so the display replays
deviations.reason: Portable software generator; the same per-trial / fixed-seed choice is kept

deviations.original: A dark CRT (0.2 cd/m^2 mean luminance) behind a circular aperture mask (p. 4746)
deviations.here: alhazen's mid-grey window, with the dots drawn on a black disc the size of the aperture (aperture_fill)
deviations.reason: alhazen's PsychoPy window background is fixed mid-grey; the disc keeps the dots bright on dark inside the aperture

deviations.here: Two discs drawn on the screen
deviations.reason: A rig with no LEDs; the targets' timing and placement on the motion axis are kept

deviations.here: Whatever eye tracker the rig file names (an EyeLink in configs/rig-monkey-example.yaml)
deviations.reason: alhazen's eye-tracker devices; the fixation window and saccade report are the same

deviations.original: Over the receptive field, at 1.3-31.4 deg eccentricity (p. 4749)
deviations.reason: There is no receptive field to match, and an unenforced fixation cannot keep a peripheral aperture peripheral

deviations.original: Monkeys: a drop of juice for a correct choice, a brief time-out for a wrong one (p. 4747)
deviations.here: The fixation point turns green (correct) or red (wrong) for 300 ms; random at 0 %, as the reward was
deviations.reason: People are not paid per trial; the information each trial gives is kept

deviations.original: Up to six blocks of the combined threshold series per neuron while isolation lasted (p. 4748)
deviations.here: One block per session (run another session for each further block); the notebook pools the runs it is given
deviations.reason: alhazen schedules a session as one plan; a recording's length decides how many are run

deviations.original: Direction-tuning series and physiological threshold series (fixation only, red fixation point) recorded MT neurons (pp. 4747-4748)
deviations.here: Not built as tasks. A recording rig adds sync lines and a recording block (configs/rig-recording-example.yaml); see docs/methods.md, 'What a recording rig adds'
deviations.reason: The behavioural task is the reusable part; recording hardware is the lab's

deviations.original: ROC analysis of each neuron's 2-s spike counts against an 'antineuron', neurometric Weibull fits, threshold ratios (pp. 4750-4753)
deviations.here: Implemented in britten1992.analysis and the notebook, but run only when a run's trials table carries spike counts (spike_count); nothing is computed or shown without a recording
deviations.reason: No recording, no neurometric function; the code is ready for one
